description: Single-panel SEM micrograph belonging to Fig. 10, which the caption attributes to Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steels held at 600 °C: (a) 9Al-20Mn-1C and (b) 9Al-30Mn-1C. Only one micrograph was supplied for this figure group, and it carries no printed panel letter, magnification or detector label; a 20 µm scale bar sits in the lower-right corner. The field shows an equiaxed polygonal grain structure outlined by dark grain boundaries, with individual grains several times longer than the 20 µm scale bar. The defining feature is a set of fine, closely spaced parallel striations inside every grain; each grain hosts striations of a single orientation, and the striation direction changes from grain to grain, so neighbouring grains show clearly different striation families. A few small (µm-scale) dark rounded particles/voids are scattered, several at grain boundaries and triple junctions. No discrete second-phase precipitates are resolvable at this magnification, and no phase, composition or condition labels are printed on the panel. The caption and citing text interpret these striations plus precipitates as κ + α in 9Al-20Mn-1C and κ-carbides in 9Al-30Mn-1C; the image alone does not confirm phase identity.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar (lower right) showing equiaxed polygonal grains; fine parallel striations run in one direction per grain and change orientation between grains; a few small dark rounded particles/voids sit at boundaries and triple junctions. No panel letter, magnification or detector label is printed, so the image cannot be assigned to (a) 9Al-20Mn-1C or (b) 9Al-30Mn-1C from the pixels alone.

observations.observation: The figure is a single SEM micrograph with a 20 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner; no panel letter, magnification value or detector (SE/BSE) label is printed on the image.
The microstructure consists of equiaxed polygonal grains separated by dark grain boundaries; most grains span several times the length of the 20 µm scale bar.
Fine, closely spaced parallel striations occur inside the grains, with one striation orientation per grain; the striation direction changes from grain to grain.
A small number of dark, rounded µm-scale particles/voids are scattered over the field, several located on grain boundaries and at triple junctions.
No discrete second-phase precipitates are resolvable as separate particles at the magnification of this micrograph, and no phase labels or arrows are printed on the panel.
The caption states the figure depicts grain striations and κ/α precipitates for (a) 9Al-20Mn-1C and (b) 9Al-30Mn-1C at 600 °C.
The citing text states that the austenite in both alloys featured parallel striations with different directions in each grain (Fig. 10).
The citing text interprets the striations plus precipitates as probably κ + α in 9Al-20Mn-1C (with apparent continuity with the grains) and as only κ-carbides in 9Al-30Mn-1C.
The citing text states that the two microstructures shown in Fig. 10 kept the same hardness as their respective hot-rolled variants instead of being strengthened by the high amount of κ-carbides.
The citing text states that the nature of the striation morphology requires deeper investigation, i.e. its origin is not established by this figure.
